title: Resurrection of the Dead
definition: Resurrection of the Dead refers to God’s promised future life and restoration.
summary: Resurrection of the Dead refers to God’s promised future life and restoration.
christFocus: Christ’s resurrection guarantees the life and restoration promised to His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Resurrection of the Dead places present life under the future God has promised. The future of believers is bodily, relational, holy, and centered on god’s presence.

Scripture teaches the last things to produce hope, holiness, endurance, and urgency rather than speculation. Suffering people need hope that is stronger than decay, grief, and death.

Christ stands at the center of this future. Christ’s resurrection guarantees the life and restoration promised to His people. Because of Him, believers can face death, judgment, suffering, and the future with sober confidence rather than fear.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
The coming future exposes what truly matters now. Suffering people need hope that is stronger than decay, grief, and death. Scripture’s teaching about the last things steadies the heart in a world that feels unfinished.

It also guards the Church from fear-based prophecy and careless delay. The Lord calls His people to watchfulness, holiness, comfort, mission, and trust.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let future resurrection hope strengthen present endurance. Bring this doctrine into prayer, Scripture, and daily obedience. Ask the Holy Spirit to make the truth real in your thinking, desires, relationships, and next faithful step with Christ.
